chunks: The Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام said:
"The women used to perform salat (prayer) with the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and they were instructed not to raise their heads before the men due to the tightness of the waist-wraps."

key_terms.الرِّجَالِ: the men praying in the congregation
key_terms.النَّبِيِّ: the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.النِّسَاءُ: the women participating in the congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.رُءُوسَهُنَّ: their heads, meaning raising them from sajdah (prostration)
key_terms.يُؤْمَرْنَ: they were being instructed or commanded

ai.seo_question: Why were women instructed not to raise their heads before men in congregational salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a practice observed during congregational salat (prayer) with the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It indicates an instruction given to women in the prayer setting in order to preserve modesty because of the narrowness of the men’s garments.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1176 - The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:
"The women used to pray with The Prophet (sw), and they were instructed not to raise their heads (from prostration) before the men due to the tightness of the garments”.
